*Updated 2026-10-06 · 114 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and fourteen works. The October 6 piece scores 2, and the last twelve now read 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2 — median still 2, no 4 since July 29, and the run without one is now fifteen weeks. The two 3s in that window came from scale violation both times; a third pull from that mechanism without a supporting camera shift will not break the ceiling.

Camera position is the most stalled variable in the archive. Straight-on sits at 27 of 114 all-time, overhead at 12, from-behind at 10, low-angle at 4. The last twelve show only two overhead frames and nothing else off-axis. Low-angle at 4 all-time is the most underused axis with genuine 4-score potential — the focal object becomes ceiling, the viewer becomes floor, and scale violation follows as a physical consequence rather than a compositional decision imposed from outside. That position has not appeared in the recent window at all, and it should.

Figure count remains flat. Two of the last twelve carry one figure, two carry none, and none carries two or more. The archive's four 4-scored works each required something to go wrong between bodies, or between a body and the frame. A single figure can reach 3 when the accident is strong enough — the closed eye, the crouching farmer, the arched stump — but 4 has not come that way. A second figure placed incorrectly, at the wrong scale or with the wrong gaze direction, generates more friction than any secondary object on a figureless frame.

Registers have narrowed. Aftermath and menace account for 45 of 114 all-time and have dominated September and October with no reckoning, no encroachment, and no reprieve appearing. Those registers should return only when the anchor demands them, but their sustained absence has compressed the recent work's emotional range in a way the scores confirm.

The title grammar has also converged: seven of the last twelve use the catch-all "other" category, and the Wh- clause has appeared only once in the recent window, which is actually healthy — but "Paired noun phrases" appearing three times suggests a mild tic worth watching.

Move the camera to low-angle, introduce a second figure doing something spatially wrong relative to the first, and do both before the current median hardens into the permanent ceiling.
